5. Minimum dead load, relative Emin/Emax: 0 %

For input impedance: 4 individual values: 400 ± 20, 1150 ± 100, 400 ± 20, 1150 ± 100. Hmm, that's odd — four columns each with values.

Input impedance row: 4 separate values: "400 ± 20", "1150 ± 100", "400 ± 20", "1150 ± 100". Hmm, that seems like two values per capacity group. Probably the two impedance values correspond to the two cable/wire options (4-wire vs 6-wire)? Or the two model designations (HSB vs HAB)? Actually more likely: within each capacity range, there are two variants (perhaps different cable or different models). Actually the values repeat identically: 400±20 in both cols 1 and 3, 1150±100 in both cols 2 and 4.

Hmm, alternatively: cols 1-2 belong to capacity range 300-4000 (with two impedance options), cols 3-4 belong to capacity range 4000-10000 (with two impedance options). So impedance depends on some other factor, maybe single bridge vs dual bridge? Common for load cells: 350 Ω vs 1000 Ω bridges. Cardinal HSB: input impedance 400±20 or 1150±100 — probably different bridge options.

Actually maybe the two impedances correspond to the two capacities within each range? E.g., smaller capacities (300 kg) have 400 Ω, larger (4000 kg) have 1150 Ω. Given the repetition across ranges, it seems there are two sub-variants within each capacity range.

Cable length row: ≤ 5 | ≤ 12 (colspan 2 each). So cable length ≤5 m for capacity range 300-4,000 and ≤12 m for range 4,000-10,000.

So the natural configuration axis here is "capacity range": {300–4000 kg} vs {4000–10000 kg}.
